narrative.executive_summary: The scan of nordmsp-lab ran 16 checks; all 16 failed, and 20 requirements are recorded as not satisfied. Most urgent: the admin console accepts the default admin/admin login (CHK-IDP-004). High-severity gaps follow: the newest backup snapshot is far too old (CHK-BAK-001), two accounts lack MFA (CHK-IDP-001), SSH offers password authentication and direct root login (CHK-SSH-001, CHK-SSH-002), outdated TLS versions are accepted (CHK-TLS-001), and fixable critical vulnerabilities remain in running images (CHK-VUL-001). Medium and low findings concern the asset inventory (CHK-AST-001), the incident response plan (CHK-DOC-001, CHK-DOC-002), identity settings (CHK-IDP-002, CHK-IDP-003), log retention (CHK-LOG-001), certificate validity and HTTPS handling (CHK-TLS-002, CHK-TLS-003) and SSH attempt limits (CHK-SSH-003).

gaps.why_it_matters: The law requires access control policies and, in the implementing regulation, that authentication credentials are changed initially, at predefined intervals and whenever compromise is suspected. The check logged in to the admin console with the username admin and the password admin and received HTTP status 200, whereas the expected result is that such a login is not accepted. A default credential that is publicly known gives anyone who reaches the console full administrative control of the system, so every other access control measure can be bypassed.
remediation: Change the password of the 'admin' account so that the default admin/admin combination is no longer accepted, matching the expected result accepted: false.
Re-run the check to confirm the admin console rejects the default credentials.
Apply the credential-change rule described in point 11.6.2 to this account: change credentials initially, at predefined intervals, and upon suspicion of compromise.

gaps.why_it_matters: NIS2 requires business continuity including backup management, and the implementing regulation requires that backup copies of data are maintained. The scan found only 1 snapshot, with the newest dated 2025-06-01 and reported as 480 days old (age_hours 11542.6), against an expected max_age_hours of 26. Recovery from an incident would therefore fall back to a very old copy, and everything created since that snapshot would be lost.
remediation: Run and verify a new backup so a fresh snapshot exists for the target.
Schedule backups so that the newest snapshot always stays within the expected max_age_hours value of 26.
Monitor the age of the newest snapshot and alert when it approaches that expected value.

gaps.why_it_matters: The directive and the implementing regulation call for multi-factor or continuous authentication for access to network and information systems, and specifically strong authentication such as MFA for privileged and system administration accounts. The scan observed two accounts without MFA, kari.admin and ola.tech, and that new accounts are not required to enrol OTP (new_users_must_enrol_otp: false). A stolen or guessed password alone is then enough to sign in, and the gap will keep growing as new accounts are created.
remediation: Enrol MFA for the accounts kari.admin and ola.tech so that users_without_mfa becomes empty.
Set new_users_must_enrol_otp to true so that newly created accounts are required to enrol OTP.
Re-run the check to confirm both expected values are met.

gaps.why_it_matters: Access control policies must ensure the strength of authentication is appropriate to the classification of the asset being accessed. The SSH server offers both password and publickey authentication, while the check expects password, keyboard-interactive and none not to be offered. Because password login remains available, remote attackers can attempt to guess credentials for shell access instead of being limited to key-based authentication.
remediation: Reconfigure the SSH server so password authentication is no longer offered, leaving publickey as the offered method.
Ensure keyboard-interactive and none are likewise not offered, as listed under expected not_offered.
Confirm the required users hold working public keys before the change, then re-run the check.

gaps.why_it_matters: The implementing regulation requires administration privileges to be individualised and restricted to the highest extent possible. The scan found PermitRootLogin set to 'yes', while the expected setting is 'no'. Direct root login means administrative actions are performed through a shared, fully privileged account, so actions cannot be traced to an individual and one compromised credential grants complete control of the host.
remediation: Set PermitRootLogin to 'no' in the SSH server configuration, matching the expected value.
Ensure administrators have individual accounts with the privilege escalation they need before applying the change.
Restart or reload the SSH service and re-run the check.

gaps.why_it_matters: NIS2 requires policies and procedures on the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption. The server accepts TLSv1, TLSv1.1 and TLSv1.2, whereas the profile expects a minimum version of TLSv1.2. Because the two older versions are still accepted, a client or an attacker positioned in the network path can negotiate the weaker protocol instead of the stronger one, undermining the protection of traffic in transit.
remediation: Configure the server to refuse TLSv1 and TLSv1.1 so that accepted versions start at the expected min_version TLSv1.2.
Re-run the check to confirm only versions at or above TLSv1.2 are accepted.

gaps.why_it_matters: The directive covers vulnerability handling, and the implementing regulation requires appropriate measures to manage vulnerabilities, that critical vulnerabilities are addressed without undue delay, and that security patches are applied within a reasonable time after they become available. Across 6 images scanned, the check found fixable CRITICAL vulnerabilities in nginx:1.20 (17), quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.3 (4), nis2lab-backup (3) and grafana/loki:3.5.1 (2), with no accepted risks recorded, and nginx:1.20 flagged under os_end_of_support. Fixes already exist for these issues, so the exposure is avoidable.
remediation: Update the affected images (nginx:1.20, quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.3, nis2lab-backup, grafana/loki:3.5.1) to versions where the listed fixable CRITICAL CVEs are resolved.
Give priority to nginx:1.20, which carries 17 findings and is listed under os_end_of_support.
Where a fix cannot be applied immediately, record the item explicitly under accepted_risks with a rationale, and re-run the check to confirm no unaccepted fixable CRITICAL findings remain.

gaps.why_it_matters: Asset management under NIS2, detailed in point 12.4.1, requires a complete, accurate, up-to-date and consistent inventory of assets. Of the running services (backup, host, idp, legacy-web, logs, web), three are not in the inventory: backup, legacy-web and logs. Services that are not recorded are unlikely to be patched, monitored or included in incident handling, and the expected result is that no undeclared services remain.
remediation: Add backup, legacy-web and logs to the asset inventory with their owners and relevant details.
Confirm the inventory matches the running services list so that undeclared_services is empty.
Re-run the check after updating the inventory.

gaps.why_it_matters: Article 23(4) sets out staged reporting of significant incidents, beginning with an early warning without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of the incident. The document incident-response.md does not mention the 24h early warning, the 72h incident notification, the one-month final report or the CSIRT contact. Without these in the plan, staff handling an incident have no written instruction on what to report, when, or to whom.
remediation: Add sections to incident-response.md covering the 24h early warning, the 72h incident notification and the one-month final report.
Record the CSIRT contact in the same document.
Re-run the check to confirm all four expected items are mentioned.

gaps.why_it_matters: Point 11.6.2 requires credential reset and blocking of users after a predefined number of unsuccessful log-in attempts. In the staff realm, bruteForceProtected is false even though a failureFactor of 30 is configured, so the blocking behaviour never takes effect. Attackers can therefore make unlimited password guesses against staff accounts without being stopped.
remediation: Set bruteForceProtected to true on the staff realm so the configured failureFactor takes effect.
Re-run the check to confirm brute-force protection is enabled.

gaps.why_it_matters: Both cited points of the implementing regulation require authentication strength appropriate to the classification of the asset being accessed. The scan found passwordPolicy set to null and min_length 0, meaning no minimum password length is enforced, against an expected minimum length of at least 12. Users can therefore choose very short passwords that are quick to guess.
remediation: Configure a password policy that sets a minimum length of at least 12, replacing the current empty passwordPolicy.
Re-run the check to confirm the minimum length is enforced.

gaps.why_it_matters: Incident handling under NIS2 and point 3.2.5 require logs to be maintained and backed up for a predefined period. Central logs are configured with retention_period 1w, that is retention_days 7, while the profile expects min_retention_days of 90. Evidence needed to investigate an incident detected later is therefore deleted before it can be examined.
remediation: Increase the central log retention setting from retention_days 7 to at least the expected min_retention_days of 90.
Ensure storage is sized for the longer retention and that logs are backed up as required by point 3.2.5.
Re-run the check to confirm the retention setting.

gaps.why_it_matters: NIS2 requires policies and procedures on the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption. The certificate has not_before 2024-01-01 and not_after 2025-01-01 and is reported as expired, with days_left of -633 against an expected min_days_remaining of 14. An expired certificate causes client warnings or failures and removes the assurance that users are connecting to the genuine service.
remediation: Issue and install a current certificate for the service to replace the one with not_after 2025-01-01.
Set up renewal and alerting so the certificate is replaced before it falls below the expected min_days_remaining of 14.
Re-run the check to confirm the certificate is valid.

gaps.why_it_matters: Under the cryptography and encryption requirement, traffic should be protected in transit. The scan found that plain HTTP returns http_status 200 with no location redirect and no Strict-Transport-Security header, while the expected result is that HTTP redirects to HTTPS and HSTS is set. Users and clients can therefore continue over unencrypted HTTP, exposing credentials and data to interception.
remediation: Configure the web service so plain HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS instead of returning a 200 response.
Add the Strict-Transport-Security header to HTTPS responses.
Re-run the check to confirm both expected values are met.

gaps.why_it_matters: Incident handling under Article 21(2)(b) depends on documentation that reflects the current environment. The document incident-response.md was last reviewed on 2023-02-14, 1319 days ago, against an expected maximum review age of 365 days. Contacts, roles and steps in a long-unreviewed plan are likely to be out of date when an incident occurs.
remediation: Review and update incident-response.md, then record the new review date.
Set a recurring review so the document's age stays within the expected maximum of 365 days.
Re-run the check after the review date is updated.

gaps.why_it_matters: Access control policies under Article 21(2)(i) include limiting how easily credentials can be guessed. The SSH server has MaxAuthTries set to 10, while the check expects at most 4. A higher allowance lets an attacker make more guesses per connection before being disconnected, making password-guessing attempts more efficient.
remediation: Reduce MaxAuthTries in the SSH server configuration to 4 or lower.
Restart or reload the SSH service and re-run the check.
